title: Why the Kiosk Calendar Finally Shows the Whole School Day | vitalii.no
description:
A child's calendar cell on the family kiosk used to show homework notes and nothing else. A day with four lessons and only one homework task looked like a day with just one subject — the rest of the school day was simply invisible. The homework line itself also used to scroll sideways, which made it hard to read at a glance.

KioskFrame.tsx gained a function that merges the day's school events with its homework notes: for every subject in that day's timetable, it attaches the matching homework note if one exists, or renders a bare subject tile if not. A new auto-shrinking line component replaced the old sideways-scrolling animation, reducing font size before ever truncating with an ellipsis.

A day's kiosk cell now shows every subject a child has that day, in the real timetable order, with homework attached where it exists. The homework line finally sits still instead of sliding — it shrinks to fit, down to 55% size, before it's ever cut off.
